title: Took vg-paradigms release 2026.10.23 by its auto subscription
body:
The dry run broke nothing: no rule it would newly break, no license it would block. What moved:
- ~ checks.commands: A project's commands come first from a proper build environment: its build tool (cargo, uv, bun) in a runtime pinned by the language's own files (rust-toolchain.toml, .python-version, packageManager). What that doesn't cover is, in order of preference: a custom CLI (the most portable, a Rust project's `cargo xtask`), idempotent shell scripts (the least effort), or Nix commands. No task runner (just, make) sits between. The project declares each check as a tend test or gate with the command it runs, which the hooks, agents, other machines and release checks run. A flake's dev shell is optional (system libraries, or a project that's Nix anyway): commands run inside it with its environment cached until flake.nix or flake.lock changes. `nix flake check` is for outputs that are Nix themselves (machine configurations, NixOS VM tests).
- ~ checks.contract: Tests and benchmarks follow tend's check contract: the schema `tend:check/1` (`tend code checks --schema`: kind, command, needs, unit, gates' condition and level), with needs from the estate's capability vocabulary (thalam's export). Exit codes follow the automake convention: 0 passed, 1 failed, 77 skipped because it can't run here (the reason on stderr's last line), 99 broken. Results go to the file tend names in TEND_RESULTS when it's set: JUnit XML for tests, Bencher's BMF for benchmarks. A command never prompts, runs on the pinned runtime with `--locked`, and is idempotent if it changes anything; a benchmark runs on the real machine, alone, best of N, and its gates compare it with the same machine's earlier runs (`<= 1.05 * previous`). Gates are tend's, not the project's code.
- ~ ci.closed: A project closed to contributions (the default) has no CI: no workflows, and GitHub Actions turned off. Its declared tests and gates run in git hooks (tend's checks and the tests a change reaches before a commit, all of them before a push), and checks for other systems run on your own machines through Nix remote builders. A check no machine here can run is the exception: its workflow stays, with a decision in the journal that waives ci.closed and says why.
- ~ deps.pinned: A dependency on another of your projects is pinned in what's committed: a released version, a git tag or a revision, never a path to a sibling checkout. To develop two projects together, override it locally and uncommitted (Cargo's `[patch]` in your own .cargo/config.toml, a flake's `--override-input`, `bun link`). The dependency is a subscription: its releases arrive as that project's subscription says, and moving the pin runs this project's checks first.
- guidance changed
